_about: Pronunciation lexicon: one file per project, versioned. It rewrites the TTS text only; the visible text is never changed. Every entry says who decided it. A changed entry is a new line (retext), never a patch of an old take. No ASR, no model produced any entry.
tashkeel_source: writer-stage (hand-written). A diacritizer is a model: it enters only after a recorded owner decision (references/pronunciation.md).

entries.written: <name as it appears in the script>
entries.tts_text: <the same name with the vowels the engine should say>
entries.reading: <plain-letter note of the sound, for the owner's ear check>
entries.note: stress, long vowel, the letter that is easy to misread

entries.written: <foreign word in Arabic letters, e.g. a place or a brand>
entries.tts_text: <respelled in Arabic letters the engine reads as the source sound, vowelled>
entries.reading: <how it sounds in the source language>
entries.note: if the visible text glosses the word, the gloss stays in the visible text only

numbers.policy: Every digit is written out as words in tts_text, in the grammatical case the sentence needs (gender of the counted noun, case ending). Years, ordinals, times and decimals are listed here once so every line reads them alike.

examples.tts_text: <the number in words matching the counted noun's gender>

check: Offline only: a script lists every written form of the script text that is in this file and every digit or Latin letter left in tts_text. Listening is the owner's.
